Shabbos Parshas Eikev,

23 Menachem Av 5728

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section discusses the obligation to recite one hundred blessings daily, derived from the verse "What does Hashem ask of you," and questions the connection between the word "Mah" (what) and "Me'ah" (one hundred).

translations.translation: "And now, Israel, what does Hashem your G-d ask of you, but to fear [Him]..."
And it is brought in the Gemara:
A person is obligated to recite one hundred blessings every day, as it is said, "And now, Israel, what (Mah) does Hashem your G-d ask of you,"
Do not read it as "Mah" but rather as "Me'ah" (one hundred).
And it needs to be understood,
for "Mah" and "Me'ah" are two different matters,
and furthermore,
they are opposites,
for the word "Mah" indicates that the matter
(being discussed)
is something small,
and "Me'ah" is
a large number, even the completeness of number
[And particularly according to what is explained in Chassidus,
that which is added,
in "Me'ah" over "Mah" is the letter Aleph, the letters of "Peleh" (wonder),
the Ohr HaSovev (Surrounding Light) that is above the chain of descent].
Also, one must understand what the Tur writes
in the name of Rav Natronai Gaon,
that this requirement to recite one hundred blessings every day is an enactment of King Dovid,
as it is written,
"The utterance of the man who was raised on high,"
"On high" (Al) in gematria is 100,
and the homiletic interpretation "Do not read it as Mah but rather as Me'ah" is merely an asmachta (support).
And the reason Dovid enacted the recitation of one hundred blessings is
(as the Tur writes there)

because every day one hundred souls from Israel would die, and they did not know why they were dying, until he investigated and understood through the Holy Spirit, and he instituted one hundred blessings each day.
And it needs to be understood,
that from the fact that the obligation to recite one hundred blessings each day is derived
(in the manner of an asmachta)
from the verse "What does Hashem your G-d ask of you," in which it is stated
(in the continuation of the verse)
"to fear Hashem your G-d... and to love Him,"
it is understood
that in order to come to fear Hashem and love Him, it is through one hundred blessings,
and nevertheless, for many generations
(all the time that one hundred souls did not die each day)
they did not institute the recitation of one hundred blessings each day.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the concept of blessing as a drawing down from the hidden world to the revealed world, connecting the two Names of Hashem.

translations.translation: B)
And this will be understood based on what is explained in the discourses that elucidate the matter of blessings
in the explanation of the verse,
"Blessed... from the world and until the world,"
that the matter of blessing is a drawing down from the hidden world (Alma d'Itkasiya) to the revealed world (Alma d'Itgalya),
for regarding the Sefiros, it is the drawing down from Binah
(the hidden world)
to Malchus
(the revealed world).
And regarding the Names, it is the drawing down of the upper Havayah into the lower Havayah.
And the connection of Binah and Malchus to the two Names Havayah is,
for the upper Havayah is Sovev (Surrounding),
and in Binah there is the revelation of Kesser
(Sovev),
and the lower Havayah is Memaleh (Filling),
which shines in Malchus.
And the matter of blessing is the drawing down of the revelation of the upper Havayah into the lower Havayah.
And it is explained in the discourses,
that the drawing down of the upper Havayah into the lower Havayah, which is accomplished through blessing, is in a manner that the two Names become joined together.
And although "Havayah Havayah" has a pause-trope (psik taima) between them,
the pause-trope is not a complete interruption
(like other separations),
and furthermore, it is brought in the Pardes
that the pause-trope between the two Names Havayah unites and connects them,
through the blessing,
the connection of the two Names is a complete connection and union.
